reason: This passage from Exodus 14 depicts the crossing of the Red Sea. While the Israelite people complain to Moses about being brought out of Egypt (they fear death in the wilderness and regret being freed from slavery), Yahweh does not voice any complaint about the people. Instead, Yahweh takes protective and salvific action: looking down on the Egyptian camp, confusing them, fighting on behalf of the Israelites, parting the sea, and ultimately saving Israel while destroying the Egyptians. Yahweh's role in this passage is active and redemptive, not one of complaint or displeasure with the people.
